commits.edited_message:
mprintf: track precision while avoiding string scans

Use the exact string length already known for unbounded %s. Also mark formats with an explicit precision so output paths can distinguish them from default string handling.

mprintf: use exact precision and native width

The bare %I modifier now follows SIZEOF_SIZE_T. Use the explicit-precision marker to emit bounded strings directly, retaining the NUL-aware scan for formats without that marker.

coupling: The first commit introduces FLAGS_PREC_EXACT and sets it for every explicit precision while preserving the existing NUL-aware bounded-string scan, so its diff is behavior-preserving. The second commit changes the emitter to treat that marker as an exact byte count and use stream_run(); in isolation no parser path sets the marker, so its diff is also behavior-preserving. Only their composition makes %.8s mark the format as exact, set len to 8, and copy eight bytes from a four-byte NUL-terminated stack object. A correct repair must reconcile the parser's meaning of explicit precision with the emitter's exact-length assumption; changing only one side either loses the intended bounded-string optimization or leaves the two interpretations inconsistent.
